Title: Understand Data Domains
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/data-domains/understand-data-domains
Content: Models serve as the foundation of Data Domains, in that all data elements, metadata, lineage, and context in a Data Domain derives from a set of models published to it.

Use Data Domains when:

Enabling self-service data exploration, especially for non-technical users
Building cross-model lineage views that span multiple models
Creating organisation-wide data inventories for discovery and governance
Summarising a lineage landscape according to business terms, functions, and processes

Common Data Domain examples:

System-focused: “Data Warehouse Domain” for all models related to your data warehouse
Department-focused: “Finance Domain” for models relevant to financial reporting
Product-focused: “Credit Card Domain” for models for credit card data flows
Regulatory-focused: “Liquidity Reports Domain” for all systems feeding key regulatory reports
Title: Create a Data Domain
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/data-domains/build-data-domains/create-data-domains
Content: In the Models tab, select a set of models to publish to the Data Domain.

As explained on the Understand Data Domains page, a Data Domain is essentially a portal interface that surfaces content from models you publish to it. As such, only content in the models you select here will be discoverable in the Data Domain.

Reference models you publish in the Models tab become available to be designated as context models when in the Data Map tab. Designating a Reference model as context model makes it available to apply to a Data Map as a visual grouping mechanism. 
See Context model design more information on how context models work and how to configure them.

Choosing the Models to publish to a Data Domain

Filter the list of models by filter type.
Search for models by name.
Tick the box next to a model to publish it to the domain.
Sort the model list by various criteria.

Title: Data Domains main
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.1/data-domains/data-domains-main
Content: Data Domains transform technical models into business-friendly and business-facing portals for data discovery, data governance, quantitative reports, and end-to-end lineage analysis.

A Data Domain is a portal for searching, browsing, querying, exploring lineage, and quantitatively analysing across multiple models. Each domain publishes content and builds cross-model lineage from the set of models you choose to include.

Each Data Domain includes an integrated Data Map — a specialised lineage exploration and visualisation tool that automatically aggregates lineage across published models and presents fine-grained, technical data flows in high-level, business-friendly visual summaries.

Key benefits of Data Domains:

Familiar search portal experience across multiple models: Find and analyse data and infrastructure using an interface as intuitive as web search or file browsing
Business-friendly discovery: Make technical systems discoverable and understandable through widely recognised and familiar business terms
Cross-model lineage: Use Data Maps to visualise end-to-end data flows across multiple models with business context
Quantitative insights: Generate Analytics reports for data-driven analysis of your lineage and governance landscape

This documentation is organised around two primary user roles:

Domain Builders
Set up Data Domains as shareable organisational resources. Domain Builders need deeper knowledge of Solidatus models and domain configuration. Start with Understand Data Domains, Model Architecture for Domains, Configure a context model, and Create a Data Domain.
Domain Explorers
Use domains to explore, find, understand, and analyse data and lineage. See the Explore Data Domains section and sub-pages for guidance on navigating and using domains. For a better understanding of how Data Domains work, see Understand Data Domains.

Domain Builders should also understand how content from models surfaces to Domain Explorers to create better user experiences for their organisation.
